Neil Ortlieb (BB Pro League) |other_names=ORBITRON |from=Waterloo, ON, Canada |speed=25mph |power=8x 8S LiPo batteries |drive=2x Brushless motors |weight=250lbs |stats=Orbitron_PG_stats.png|other_events=BattleBots Pro League (2026)}} '''Orbitron''', sometimes stylized as '''ORBITRON''', is a [[Heavyweights|heavyweight]] robot built by the eponymous [[Team Orbitron]], which has fought at ''[[BattleBots]]'' [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''Proving Ground'']], ''[[BattleBots FaceOffs|FaceOffs]],'' and also competed in the 2026 [[BattleBots Pro League|''BattleBots Pro League'']]. The design intent of Orbitron is to make AI and software automation competitive in combat robotics. Although teams have attempted varying levels of computer-based enhancements before, Orbitron is the first to integrate computer control with automated driving and strategy algorithms. To enable this, the team uses a high-mounted camera and a desktop computer as their driver station, which runs computer vision algorithms to track robots in the arena and make driving decisions. Orbitron is mechanically optimized to utilize the advantages of software control. The drivetrain is tuned for speed and maneuverability beyond what human drivers can easily control, using high-power brushless power systems and bottom-mounted magnets to maximize speed, torque, and traction. Four-wheel drive ensures that all downforce is converted to effective traction, increasing the robot's ability to move quickly. Additionally, Orbitron splits its weapon weight into two, counter-rotating [[Vertical Spinners|vertical spinners]] to maintain high damage output while eliminating gyroscoptic precession effects while turning. This allows for full speed maneuvers regardless of how fast the weapons are spinning, weapon redundancy, and more effective comboing of hits (as one spinner can be charging while the other is used offensively). Orbitron also has a dedicated [[self-righting mechanism]] to recover if flipped over. The team describes Orbitron as a "modernized [[Counter Revolution]]"Public message from Steven Szczeszynski in the Out of the Arena Discord server, which initially inspired the twin-vertical spinner design. Team Orbitron are made up of students from the University of Waterloo, many of which have prior experience and acheivements with FIRST Robotics. They uploaded an application video in mid 2023.https://uwbattlebots.notion.site/UW-Battlebots-Team-Orbitron-5916d5857de348c98ce4910e1b5d63e5 For their appearances at ''BattleBots: Destruct-A-Thon'', they were joined by members from [https://www.youtube.com/@theHacksmith Hacksmith Industries]. Their YouTube channel, which boasts over 14 million subscribers, uploaded a video documenting the process on September 23, 2023.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=suv6DtRLnMw First AUTONOMOUS BattleBot!?!] A video documenting the fight and the problems before and during the fight was uploaded September 30, 2023.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TiSpihZnq4E&t=937s Our BATTLEBOT FIGHT! (Orbitron VS Roundhouse)] Orbitron fought [[RoboGym Robotics|RoboGym Robotics']] new horizontal spinner [[Roundhouse]] on the weekend of August 26-27, 2023, where it lost on both occasions. Following these losses, Team Orbitron set about a full rebuild of their robot. New features included TPU plastic sides to better absorb side attacks, as well as shock mounting on their speed controllers. Its new disks weighed 27lbs and could be swapped out or paired with bars weighing 17lbs.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/438752241042849793/1214634997793816676 Public messages from Steven Szczeszynski in the Out of the Arena Discord server] Orbitron now also sported magnets on its underside. It signed up for the weekend of March 9-10, 2024, where it twice defeated ''Proving Ground'' rookie [[Disarray]] to earn its first career wins. ''BattleBots'' co-founder [[Trey Roski]] effectively confirmed Orbitron's inclusion into the next televised season in a March 2024 episode of the ''Outside of the Box'' podcast, pending the season being green-lit and its team being able to compete.[https://youtu.be/OenyAKHZnUo?feature=shared BattleBots Proving Grounds Discussion on Outside of the Box] In the meantime, Orbitron was confirmed to be competing in ''[[BattleBots FaceOffs]]'' in November 2024. The team made alterations to Orbitron's armor, incorporating a dedicated anti-horizontal wedge in anticipation of fighting [[Tombstone]] and [[Valkyrie]], as well as additional magnets and time spent adapting their AI software. In testing, Team Orbitron designed a 45lb model of Tombstone to test their AI software against, called '''Tombclone'''.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BZX8cgkHxCE Battlebots Face-Off's MOST DESTRUCTIVE WEEK YET!] Orbitron returned for a special ''FaceOffs'' group named 'Battle of the Verts', where it fought [[JackPot]], [[Magnitude]] and [[Terrortops]] across July 25-27, 2025. Though its electronics remained the same, Orbitron's frame was redesigned from the ground up. One major design change for this version of the machine concerned its shorter self-righting arm, which the team hoped would help it recover from being flipped more efficiently.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/438752241042849793/1398754179228635217 Public message from Steven Szczeszynski in the Out of the Arena Discord server] This build of Orbitron was displayed at ''[[BattleBots: Destruct-A-Thon|Destruct-A-Thon]]'' from late 2025, alongside [[Ginsu]] and Tombstone.https://www.facebook.com/roamingrobots/posts/pfbid0294fGnSaYQW3Y71Hbewei1enWCsotEaPuH99o1ZPqb4xrBDE8FztjWYyG3YMrxrQMl Orbitron and its team will compete in the inaugural ''BattleBots Pro League'' in 2026 alongside 23 other competitors. For this tournament, the team opted for minimal upgrades, though widened Orbitron's wheelbase for better maneuvrability.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6i-4Y0BF6BI Week 2 Behind The Scenes At BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE] Orbitron_Pro_League_Test_Box_2026.png|Orbitron undergoing weapon tests during the 2026 ''Pro League''. '''Orbitron vs. Roundhouse (8/26/2023)'''

Orbitron's first ever ''BattleBots'' fight came in ''Proving Ground'', where it fought [[Roundhouse]].

[[File:Roundhouse Orbitron 1 1.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron strikes the front of Roundhouse.]]Orbitron box-rushed Roundhouse with both its disks up to speed as the [[RoboGym Robotics]] entry turned to meet it head-on, losing parts of its decorative armor on impact. Roundhouse's flamethrower threatened to toast Orbitron, who continued to buffet against its front.

[[File:Roundhouse vs Orbitron 1 2.png|thumb|Orbitron suddenly stops working.]]Just over twenty seconds into the fight, Roundhouse turned to spin up its weapon but left itself vulnerable to Orbitron's disks. The Canadian rookies struck the rear of Roundhouse, tearing away more decorative panels and halting its 50lb weapon again. Orbitron's controller suddenly disconnected and the robot stopped working.Public message from Wilson Wang of Orbitron in the Out of the Arena Discord server{{Quote|Oh no... come on Orbitron!|Bil Dwyer as Orbitron stops working}}
[[File:Roundhouse vs Orbitron 1 KO.png|left|thumb|Roundhouse strikes Orbitron.]][[File:Orbitron post fight 1 PG.png|thumb|Damage to Orbitron, post-fight.]]Roundhouse took full advantage of this turn of fortune, swiping its opponent's side and causing it to spin away into the corner. Roundhouse continued to strike the defenceless Orbitron before lingering in the blue starting square.

A count-out began soon as Orbitron suffered a debut loss by knockout in under ninety seconds. |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Roundhouse (8/27/2023)'''

Orbitron fought [[Roundhouse]] for a second time the following day.

[[File:Roundhouse vs Orbitron 2 hit 1.gif|left|thumb|Roundhouse strikes Orbitron.]]Orbitron was once again quick to chase its foe at the start of the match, but between the slippery floor of the [[BattleBox]] and Roundhouse's much improved spinner, Orbitron accidentally drifted side-on into the massive horizontal blade. A second hit to the side mangled its side armor and sent it careening into the screws, and as it began to crabwalk away Roundhouse delivered a third powerful shot which launched it back against the screws and caused one of its vertical disks to bounce off the floor.

[[File:Roundhouse vs Orbitron 2 hit 2.gif|thumb|The knockout blow.]]Now visibly struggling, Orbitron's blue disk began to falter as it tried to inch out of the corner. The Canadian bot gyroed around, turning its gold disk to face Roundhouse, but the American bot simply ripped one of Orbitron's wedges off, launching it at the Lexan so hard it bounced completely across the box afterwards. It followed this with another brutal hit which caused Orbitron to flip over, its still-spinning weapon managing to self-right it.

[[File:Orbitron Roundhouse KO fight 2.png|left|thumb|Orbitron is immobile.]][[File:Roundhouse vs Orbitron 2 burning.gif|thumb|Orbitron catches fire.]]This proved to be for naught, however, as smoke and flames began to erupt from Orbitron. It sat in the corner, immobile, as for the second fight straight it was counted out and declared the loser by knockout, ending its debut weekend 0-2. |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Disarray (3/9/2024)'''

Orbitron's return to the BattleBox came several months later, where it took on [[Disarray]] during the March 9-10, 2024 shows. For this fight, it debuted two sets of forks ahead of its front blue disk.

[[File:Orbitron Disarray 1 PG KO.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron gets the decisive blow.]]These proved effective in getting the better of Disarray early on, though the forks quickly came loose. The fight moved to the middle of the arena and as Disarray looked to retaliate, Orbitron charged with its rear disk and flung Disarray over, ripping off its right-front wheel and disabling that side of drive in the process.

[[File:Orbitron Disarray 1 KO.png|thumb|Orbitron leaves Disarray to be counted out.]]Although its left-side drive was still functional, Disarray was unable to right itself from its inverted position and Orbitron picked up its first win in this fight by knockout. In a post-fight recap video, it was discovered that Orbitron had warped part of Disarray's AR500 steel drisk weapon.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dIWXb4AUKG8 REDEMPTION at Battlebots! (Round #2)] |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Disarray (3/10/2024)'''

Orbitron fought [[Disarray]] for a second time the following day. Ahead of this fight, the team replaced their forks, replaced their bar weapon and bent their self-righting mechanism back into shape. The team also put a greater emphasis on their AI for this second battle.

Driving straight at Disarray, Orbitron got its dual disks up to speed and wasted no time ripping its opponent's fin and left-rear tire off. Orbitron then led with its forks and drove Disarray into the corner, throwing it upside-down.

[[File:Disarray Orbitron 2 KO.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron inverts Disarray again.]]With the main robot's self-righter failing, Shark Bait attempted to distract Orbitron, but suffered a hit which shattered its plastic body. Disarray was nudged back into the action by the [[Paddles|paddle hazard]], but this only served to tee the Arizona representatives up for one final shot from Orbitron's rear blade.

[[File:Orbitron vs Disarray 2 Sharkbait.gif|thumb|Orbitron goes after Disarray's minibot.]]As Disarray was counted out, Orbitron again turned its attention to Shark Bait and tore its body off completely before tearing a wheel away. A knockout was declared and Orbitron's second win of the weekend was confirmed. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | === BattleBots FaceOffs=== |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Valkyrie'''

Orbitron returned for ''BattleBots FaceOffs'' in November 2024, where it first fought the returning [[Valkyrie]] on Day 1 of [[BattleBots FaceOffs/Episode 1|Group F]]. For this battle, it was equipped with its lighter blue asymmetric bar and front plow setup, with its heavier gold-colored disk at the back for greater reach. {{Quote|You can think of our AI system as sort of a 'cruise control' for Orbitron. It'll basically steer for me, and then I still retain forward and backward controls. The way we set it up on our gamepads is pretty neat as well. We use one stick for turning, so left-right, obviously, and then we use the vertical axis to specify different AI modes. So if I push up, it'll engage one strategy algorithm. If I push down, it'll go to do a different strategy algorithm and we can cycle between different ones.|Steven Szczeszynski explains Orbitron's semi-autonomous capabilities}}[[File:Orbitron pre-fight tests Valkyrie FaceOffs.png|left|thumb|Orbitron undergoing pre-fight tests.]]During pre-match preparations, Team Orbitron troubleshooted various issues with their camera system and the robot's updated software. Tuning and testing of Orbitron involved the robot undertaking three separate sessions in the BattleBox. While generally satisfied with their results, the team found that Orbitron's lights initially caused the overhead camera to be overexposed - adversely affecting tracking - and that operating the self-righting arm was causing radio reception issues.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ni8AfNiL4g4 ORBITRON vs World's Most Destructive BATTLEBOTS (VIDEO #5/6), ''Hacksmith Industries'' (YouTube), uploaded March 27, 2025] Discussing the likelihood of Valkyrie avoiding an early box-rush, captain Steven Szczeszynski stated that the team had 'planned around this', knowing that its horizontal spinner could still pose a major threat to Orbitron. {{Quote|When there is enough energy in a horizontal spinner especially, no matter what you do, how strong you make your robot, if they get a full impulse on you, you're dead.|Steven Szczeszynski refuses to downplay Valkyrie's weapon power}}[[File:Orbitron pre-fight Valkyrie FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron pre-fight.]]Moments before the battle itself, a last-minute issue with Orbitron's AI was encountered and resolved. The pre-match strobe sequence caused many of the onboard algorithms - set up to track the movements of Valkyrie - to be 'blinded' and glitch out, requiring a manual correction.

[[File:Orbitron vs Valkyrie FaceOffs 1.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron starts in the ascendency.]]Orbitron immediately darted across the BattleBox to intercept and strike Valkyrie's left wheel guard with the blue bar. Through tracking the wheel, this attack confirmed to the team that its AI system had automatically corrected itself following the earlier glitch. With Valkyrie flung towards the top-right pocket, Orbitron began a second charge, but missed, colliding with one of the Upper Deck bumpers. This briefly left it vulnerable to attacks from Bam Singhasaneh and Leanne Cushing's machine, whose bar spinner took a small chunk out of its front plow. Orbitron followed Valkyrie as it proceeded to hit the bumper and veer deeper into the pocket. It again slammed into its opponent bar-first, flipping Valkyrie a full 360 degrees into the air, before turning around and damaging the latter's front end with the gold disk.

[[File:Orbitron vs Valkyrie FaceOffs 2.gif|thumb|Orbitron punts Valkyrie onto the Upper Deck.]]Weathering more blows from Valkyrie's slowing bar, Orbitron proceeded to pin the former against the Upper Deck bumper. More sparks flew as its blue bar clipped the back of Valkyrie, and again when Orbitron pushed the undercutter into the yellow bumper nearby. Both of Orbitron's spinners inflicted further damage as Valkyrie, launched by the latter collision, was thrown over the top of and buffeted around by them. Shards of armor included a back plate covering one of Valkyrie's battery packs. Orbitron kept corralling Valkyrie to sustain this onslaught, again capitalizing on Valkyrie driving spinner-first into the Upper Deck bumper. A final series of attacks resulted in Orbitron pinning, then flinging Valkyrie onto the Upper Deck platform.

[[File:Orbitron vs Valkyrie FaceOffs 3 KO.png|left|thumb|Orbitron leaves Valkyrie to be counted out.]]Orbitron crept around the hazard perimeter, while Valkyrie crawled and eventually stopped moving as a result of the internal damage inflicted. The Waterloo-based machine sped back towards and gyro-danced over the BattleBox center to celebrate a dominant knockout win.

Despite this commanding performance, Orbitron would not return to the Pits unscathed. Not only had its armor panels been cut and bent in various places by Valkyrie, but issues were also identified in both of its weapon systems. The motor for the bar spinner was suspected to have malfunctioned due to damage or dislodged parts, while the disk mechanism was reported to have 'something rattily' inside. |- |

'''Orbitron vs. HyperShock'''

Looking to extend its 1-0 record, Orbitron's second opponent was [[Re:MARS all:STARS BattleBots Challenge (2022)|re:MARS all:STARS 2022]] champion [[HyperShock]]. Ahead of the fight, captain Steven Szczeszynski admitted he was "absolutely terrified" of facing such an experienced opponent, highlighting HyperShock's durability. The team swapped Orbitron's front plow out for an array of forks; the outermost forks notably longer than the inner ones.

[[File:HyperShock Orbitron 1 FaceOffs.gif|thumb|Orbitron is flipped over early on.]]Orbitron instantly spun both disks up and met HyperShock head-on, colliding over the ''BattleBots'' logo. As it looked to drive away from this initial coming together, however, HyperShock cut down the angle and landed a shot to Orbitron's flank, overturning the Canadian bot. This hit also unplugged Orbitron's self-righter.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/552574228445003785/1303492592834576404 Public message by Adham Abji in the Out of the Arena Discord server]

[[File:HyperShock Orbitron OOTA KO FaceOffs.gif|left|thumb|The decisive hit.]]The AI-assisted machine lay vulnerable in the corner as its disk clanged against the arena floor, before a second impact saw the weapon stop. HyperShock's third attack forced Orbitron to topple [[Out of the Arena|out of the arena]], meaning after just eleven seconds, the fight was over and Team Orbitron were pegged back to 1-1. |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Tombstone'''

Orbitron also took on [[Tombstone]] during the group, whose team added strips of material to their spinning bar with the aim of encouraging Orbitron's AI technology to underestimate the length of their weapon.
{{Quote|This one's for [[Counter Revolution]]!|Team Orbitron pre-fight}} [[File:Tombstone shorting vs Orbitron FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron looks on as Tombstone's electronics short.]]Quickest out of its starting square, Orbitron looked to box-rush its Tombstone and collided with its front. This early attack punted Tombstone backwards as it sat vulnerable upon the screws. It also shorted the weapon system, evident by the sparks coming from its underbelly.

As the screws reversed, Orbitron's veteran opponent was free, meaning the dual-disked spinner faced it again and attacked its left flank with the lighter blue blade. Tombstone escaped, but was quickly followed by Orbitron, which now led with its heavier gold-colored disk. Orbitron got underneath and began shredding the left tire, before turning to continue the attack with its blue disk again. These attacks against the Upper Deck buckled the frame of Tombstone and caused its weapon chain to sit loose inside the cavity.
{{Quote|Orbitron is relentless here! Wow, what a great start to the fight.|Steve Judkins}} [[File:Orbitron vs Tombstone FaceOffs hits.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron's assault continues.]]Tombstone reversed away, allowing Orbitron time and space to reset. The Waterloo representatives gave chase, sweeping underneath the 2016 champions and attacking again, first with one blade and then the other. By now, Orbitron had caused visible damage to both Tombstone's drive wheels as it limped away from danger. Orbitron dealt another uppercut to the front of Tombstone which caused the defunct chain to hang out of the frame.

Suddenly, Orbitron stopped moving despite its dominance up to this point in the match; its gold disk was spinning, but its blue blade and drive were down. Just as quickly as it had stopped, however, Orbitron returned to life and the fight continued.

[[File:Orbitron high-centered vs Tombstone FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron is high-centered and unable to move.]]Orbitron continued to hunt down Tombstone, but as the former Giant Nut winner slide off Orbitron's front plow, part of the loose chain was swept underneath and became attracted to their magnets. This caused Orbitron to become high-centered and stopped the robot from moving for good.

Hardcore Robotics allowed Orbitron to be counted out, confirming a 1-2 overall finish for both robots. As Orbitron had lost their head-to-head battle with Tombstone, however, the Canadian team placed fourth in the group, though Ray Billings took time after the fight to praise Team Orbitron for their efforts.
{{Quote|Feel good about how this turned out; you did exactly what you needed to do this weekend. You belong here.|Ray Billings to Steven Szczeszynski after the fight}} |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Terrortops'''

[[File:Orbitron pre-fight vs Terrortops FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron's configuration for fighting Terrortops.|left]]Orbitron competed in a special ''FaceOffs'' group called 'Battle of the Verts' in 2025, where it first faced ''FaceOffs'' group winner [[Terrortops]]. Ahead of the fight, Team Orbitron revealed they planned to run an algorithm to specifically target the long sides of their opponent, which the team believed were a weak point. Orbitron was equipped with three long, blue wedgelets at the front and two shorter, steeper wedgelets at the rear.

[[File:Orbitron Terrortops 1 FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron stares down Terrortops.]]Orbitron exited its square first, pointing its blue disk at its opponent as Terrortops shifted back and forth. The Canadian bot showed its side to Terrortops briefly, but the former ''FaceOffs'' group winner was unable to capitalize with its lifter. {{Dialogue a-b|Steve Judkins|They're circling... feeling each other out, I think, Bil.|Bil Dwyer|Oh, it's kinda like a couple of awkward teenagers at a high school dance!|Steve and Bil comment on the cagey start to the battle}} [[File:Terrortops Orbitron flip KO.gif|thumb|Orbitron is flipped over and struck by Terrortops.|left]]Soon after, Orbitron turned sharply and showed its opposite side to Terrortops. The dinosaur-themed machine slid its forks underneath and hoisted Orbitron, avoiding both disks and succeeding in flipping it over. It also dealt a follow-up attack which sniped the gearbox for Orbitron's self-righting arm and seized the mechanism.

[[File:Orbitron vs Terrortops KO FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron lies immobile.]]Terrortops shoved Orbitron towards the short corner anticipating it to recover quickly, but it became apparent that Orbitron's self-righter was non-functional. As a result, Orbitron was immobile and Terrortops began to celebrate. Orbitron was counted out, beginning the ''FaceOffs'' group with a disappointing defeat. |- |

'''Orbitron vs. JackPot'''

Looking for its first win, Sin City Slugfest winner [[JackPot]] was Orbitron's second group opponent. Team Orbitron opted for the same wedgelet configuration as against Terrortops. The team experienced issues with their telemetry system pre-fight, but were able to get into the arena.

[[File:Orbitron vs JackPot 1 FaceOffs.png|thumb|Orbitron starts on the front foot.|left]]As JackPot and Ace left the red square, Orbitron surged towards JackPot, missing and turning sharply to face the main bot again. Orbitron charged again, this time pushing JackPot back and forcing it to gyro, lifting a side off the ground momentarily. This was enough for Orbitron to land the first blow of the battle with its blue blade. As it began circling its opponent, JackPot reversed to keep its weapon pointed at Orbitron while Ace gave chase.

[[File:Orbitron JackPot FaceOffs KO.gif|thumb|Orbitron overturns JackPot.]]Orbitron proved to be the more nimble machine as it maneuvred to the back of JackPot, ultimately hitting its right flank and peeling up its side armor. However, Orbitron also lost a front fork in this attack. Ace approached and Orbitron used its rear blade to swat the minibot away, bending its forks in the process. While Ace continued to tussle with Orbitron, JackPot itself struggled for mobility in the red square. Orbitron turned its attention back to the main bot, slicing off its right lifting arm before slamming into its back end, overturning [[Vegas Combat Robotics|Jeff Waters']] robot.

[[File:Orbitron JackPot Ace controversial hit FaceOffs.gif|thumb|The controversial hit.|left]]Orbitron backed off as Ace tried to avenge its partner, but lost one of its forks in the process. The dual-disked bot then backed into Ace, carving into its chassis and leaving the minibot incapacitated.
{{Quote|Hey, we're done! What the-?|Jeff Waters reacts as Orbitron destroys Ace}}This proved [https://battlebots.fandom.com/wiki/BattleBots_Controversies#JackPot_vs._Orbitron controversial] as Jeff Waters' team insisted they were "done" prior to what they believed to be a late hit from Orbitron. This sentiment was compounded by commentary from [[Bil Dwyer]] and [[Steve Judkins]]. {{Dialogue a-b|Steve Judkins|JackPot looks upset... Normally bots back off when their opponent's dead.|Bil Dwyer|But do the laws of mercy even apply to minibots?|Steve and Bil react to the controversial attack}} Post-fight, an enraged Jeff Waters questioned Team Orbitron's sportsmanship and encouraged their next opponent, Chad New of Magnitude, to inflict as much damage as possible. Team Orbitron doubled down on the attack, believing JackPot was attempting to remain in the battle, therefore justifying their actions.

Apologies were later exchanged between the two teams, though this was not shown in the episode's final edit.Audience recollection from [[User:Zassa2|Zassa2]] |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Magnitude'''

With the Giant Washer still obtainable, Orbitron finished the group with a clash against [[Magnitude]], piloted by veteran competitor [[Team Wazio|Chad New]].

[[File:Magnitude vs Orbitron FaceOffs 1.png|thumb|Both competitors engage in a standoff.]]The fight began and neither Magnitude nor Orbitron began quickly, with both reluctant to engage in the opening seconds. After roughly a quarter of a minute, Magnitude finally crept out of the red square, turned slowly, then slowly moved to the left side of said red square while Orbitron stayed mostly still.

[[File:Magnitude vs Orbitron FaceOffs 2.gif|left|thumb|Orbitron sends Magnitude spinning into the corner.]]Magnitude moved out of the red square for good and slowly moved closer to the barely moving Orbitron, and then the latter moved to the right of Magnitude in the hopes of getting into the side of them. Magnitude responded with the first engagement of the fight, resulting in both robots flying. Magnitude was thrown upside down which gave Orbitron an opportunity to attack, which lead to them bumping into magnitude and sending the latter into a gyro spin that sent them into one of the corners of the BattleBox.

[[File:Magnitude vs Orbitron FaceOffs KO.gif|thumb|Orbitron's decisive attack.]]Said gyro roll finally put Magnitude on its wheels, but the first successful hit from Magnitude sent it back upside down and on the back foot. A second and a more devastating third hit from Orbitron left Magnitude stuck on the arena wall. They were pushed back onto the floor by the arena paddles, which lead to more unyielding hits from Orbitron, resulting in Magnitude's eggbeater being ripped away from its frame.

Magnitude's team captain Chad New quickly signalled to the Orbitron team to call the match, leading to them being subsequently counted out. With this win, Orbitron's team would finish their ''FaceOffs'' campaign with a 2-1 record, meaning they would share the Giant Washer with Magnitude and Terrortops. |- ! style="text-align: center;" | ===BattleBots Pro League (2026)=== |- |

'''Orbitron vs. Witch Doctor'''

Orbitron took on seasoned opponents in [[Witch Doctor]] during the 2026 ''BattleBots Pro League''.

[[File:Orbitron Witch Doctor Pro League 1.png|left|thumb|Orbitron drives itself into trouble.]]While Orbitron alternated between showing its blue and gold disks to Witch Doctor, the two-time World Championship runner-up quickly spun to face its opponent. Just seconds into the fight, however, Orbitron darted forward into the arena wall, sliding one of its front wedges underneath the housing for the screws and becoming stuck.

[[File:Orbitron Witch Doctor Pro League 2.gif|thumb|Orbitron and Witch Doctor both lose ground game attachments during an exchange.]]Witch Doctor surged forward, eager to pounce on a gifted opportunity to attack. It struck the back corner of Orbitron, causing minimal damage and freeing the Canadian bot. Orbitron's centremost wedge had been curled upwards from this error, rendering it useless. The damaged Orbitron then backed into Witch Doctor, tearing away a front fork and cutting into its left-rear tire, but losing one of its rear wedges in the process. Witch Doctor was undeterred as Orbitron drove into the short corner, showing its vulnerable side to [[Team Witch Doctor|Mike]] and [[Team Witch Doctor|Andrea Gellatly]] as they dealt two hits to their flank.

[[File:Orbitron Witch Doctor Pro League KO shot.gif|left|thumb|The decisive hit.]]As Orbitron fled from the short corner, the AI-assisted machine oversteered and again showed its side to Witch Doctor. This proved a fatal mistake as the Gellatlys wasted no time in launching Orbitron through the air. Orbitron landed upside-down and had lost all power from this attack.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/438752241042849793/1529981798900301944 Explanation from Adham Abji in the Out of the Arena Discord server] As such, its self-righting mechanism was not able to function.

[[File:Orbitron Witch Doctor Pro League KO.png|thumb|Orbitron is promptly beaten.]]The Waterloo-based team tapped out after just 35 seconds, consigning them to a quick defeat in their opening fight. {{Dialogue a-b-a-b-a-b-a|Kenny Florian|We won! WE WON! WE WON!|Chris Rose|We're not gonna get replaced yet!|Sorry, Skynet! We still got it. Humans - number one! Number one!|We did it!|We did it! Humans!|And at least for one fight, human is better than AI!|Not today, AI. Not today!|Chris and Kenny humorously celebrate as their jobs remain safe}} |- |
